**Genus *Tyrannosaurus* (as of May 2024)**  

| Binomial (or provisional name) | Year / Publication | Status (as of May 2024) | Brief explanatory note |
|--------------------------------|--------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| **_Tyrannosaurus rex_** | 1905 (Osborn) | Type species; universally accepted | The only species that has a formal, uncontroversial standing. |
| **_Tyrannosaurus mcraeensis_** | 2024 (Dalman et al.) | Validly described species (most recent T‑rex‑like tyrannosaur) | New species from the Hall‑Lake Formation (NY–USA; ~73 Ma). |
| **_Tyrannosaurus imperator_** | 2022 (Greg Paul et al.) | *Proposed* second species | Paul & Co‑authors argued that the fossil record contains at least three distinct T‑rex lineages; the binomen is accepted by some but not by all researchers. |
| **_Tyrannosaurus regina_** | 2022 (Greg Paul et al.) | *Proposed* third species | Same study as above; the third lineage. |
| **_Tyrannosaurus bataar_** | 1955 (Maleev) – later reassigned | *Synonymised* with **_Tarbosaurus bataar_** | Originally named under *Tyrannosaurus*, it was re‑classified as a distinct genus in the mid‑1960s. It is still occasionally cited within discussions of the *Tyrannosaurus* lineage. |
| **_Tyrannosaurus "lanpingensis"_** | 1975 (Zhou & Gao‑style citation) | Nomen nudum (no formal diagnosis) | A tooth from Yunnan that was never followed up with a full description. |
| **_Tyrannosaurus "turpanensis"_** | 1978 (Zhou‑style) | Nomen nudum / Junior synonym | Considered a possible junior synonym of *Tarbosaurus bataar*; no formal taxonomic work was published. |
| **_Tyrannosaurus "luanchuanensis"_** | 1979–1980 | Nomen nudum | Same status as *T. turpanensis*. |
| **_Tyrannosaurus zhuchengensis_** | 2001 (Hu Chengzhi) | Uncertain / possibly junior synonym of **_Zhuchengtyrannus_** | The material was later assigned to a new genus (*Zhuchengtyrannus*); whether the species name still applies is debated. |
| **_Tyrannosaurus "shuleri"_** | 1920s–1930s | Unnamed / fragmentary material | Fragmentary remains were referred to as “*T. shuleri*”, but no formal species description was ever published. |

---

### Notes on the list

1. **Formal recognition** – Only *T. rex* and *T. mcraeensis* are presently considered valid, formally described species in the genus.  
2. **Proposed species** – *T. imperator* and *T. regina* are proposals by Gregory Paul (2022). These are not universally accepted and are sometimes treated as *T. rex* variation.  
3. **Historical typings** – *T. bataar* (now *Tarbosaurus bataar*) shows that what once fell under *Tyrannosaurus* can be reassigned when new phylogenetic evidence arises.  
4. **Nomina nuda** – The three “nomina nudum” (lanpingensis, turpanensis, luanchuanensis) were never formally described and therefore do not meet the ICZN criteria for valid species, but are still frequently cited in the literature.  
5. **Uncertain taxa** – *T. zhuchengensis* was originally in *Tyrannosaurus*, but the material was later placed into the separate genus *Zhuchengtyrannus*; it sometimes appears in older lists but its status is now doubtful.  
6. **Excluded genus** – *Nanotyrannus* is a distinct genus that was once suggested to be a junior synonym of *T. rex* but is no longer considered part of *Tyrannosaurus*.

This table therefore presents an exhaustive account of every taxon that has been formally named, proposed, or historically referenced as belonging to the genus *Tyrannosaurus* up to May 2024.

steps.text:
**Genus *Tyrannosaurus* (as of May 2024)**  

| Binomial (or provisional name) | Year / Publication | Status (as of May 2024) | Brief explanatory note |
|--------------------------------|--------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| **_Tyrannosaurus rex_** | 1905 (Osborn) | Type species; universally accepted | The only species that has a formal, uncontroversial standing. |
| **_Tyrannosaurus mcraeensis_** | 2024 (Dalman et al.) | Validly described species (most recent T‑rex‑like tyrannosaur) | New species from the Hall‑Lake Formation (NY–USA; ~73 Ma). |
| **_Tyrannosaurus imperator_** | 2022 (Greg Paul et al.) | *Proposed* second species | Paul & Co‑authors argued that the fossil record contains at least three distinct T‑rex lineages; the binomen is accepted by some but not by all researchers. |
| **_Tyrannosaurus regina_** | 2022 (Greg Paul et al.) | *Proposed* third species | Same study as above; the third lineage. |
| **_Tyrannosaurus bataar_** | 1955 (Maleev) – later reassigned | *Synonymised* with **_Tarbosaurus bataar_** | Originally named under *Tyrannosaurus*, it was re‑classified as a distinct genus in the mid‑1960s. It is still occasionally cited within discussions of the *Tyrannosaurus* lineage. |
| **_Tyrannosaurus "lanpingensis"_** | 1975 (Zhou & Gao‑style citation) | Nomen nudum (no formal diagnosis) | A tooth from Yunnan that was never followed up with a full description. |
| **_Tyrannosaurus "turpanensis"_** | 1978 (Zhou‑style) | Nomen nudum / Junior synonym | Considered a possible junior synonym of *Tarbosaurus bataar*; no formal taxonomic work was published. |
| **_Tyrannosaurus "luanchuanensis"_** | 1979–1980 | Nomen nudum | Same status as *T. turpanensis*. |
| **_Tyrannosaurus zhuchengensis_** | 2001 (Hu Chengzhi) | Uncertain / possibly junior synonym of **_Zhuchengtyrannus_** | The material was later assigned to a new genus (*Zhuchengtyrannus*); whether the species name still applies is debated. |
| **_Tyrannosaurus "shuleri"_** | 1920s–1930s | Unnamed / fragmentary material | Fragmentary remains were referred to as “*T. shuleri*”, but no formal species description was ever published. |

---

### Notes on the list

1. **Formal recognition** – Only *T. rex* and *T. mcraeensis* are presently considered valid, formally described species in the genus.  
2. **Proposed species** – *T. imperator* and *T. regina* are proposals by Gregory Paul (2022). These are not universally accepted and are sometimes treated as *T. rex* variation.  
3. **Historical typings** – *T. bataar* (now *Tarbosaurus bataar*) shows that what once fell under *Tyrannosaurus* can be reassigned when new phylogenetic evidence arises.  
4. **Nomina nuda** – The three “nomina nudum” (lanpingensis, turpanensis, luanchuanensis) were never formally described and therefore do not meet the ICZN criteria for valid species, but are still frequently cited in the literature.  
5. **Uncertain taxa** – *T. zhuchengensis* was originally in *Tyrannosaurus*, but the material was later placed into the separate genus *Zhuchengtyrannus*; it sometimes appears in older lists but its status is now doubtful.  
6. **Excluded genus** – *Nanotyrannus* is a distinct genus that was once suggested to be a junior synonym of *T. rex* but is no longer considered part of *Tyrannosaurus*.

This table therefore presents an exhaustive account of every taxon that has been formally named, proposed, or historically referenced as belonging to the genus *Tyrannosaurus* up to May 2024.
